content.comment_body: I am using [product_name] app [version_no] for Android connected to [product_name] [version_no]. How should I configure a switch button so it functions as a push button? The network input in my program is labeled as [version_no]. Currently, it works as a switch but not as a push button with the app.

The [product_name] app only sends bits as static signals (switches), not as dynamic signals (push buttons). You need to handle this within the [product_name] program. Read the signal with a network input (in your case [version_no]). This signal then triggers your desired function, such as a pulse relay. Use a network output at the same address ([version_no]) and connect it to a LOW block.
Hello [user_name], From the Device Overview page in the app, go to the Control Page. Add a new control using the + sign, then add a button. After that, follow the steps provided in the attachment.
Hello [user_name], Thank you for your explanation. Unfortunately, this cannot be found in the manual. It's disappointing that [company_name] does not include this information.

Hello [user_name], You're welcome. Actually, I should thank you for all the knowledge you've generously shared with us over time. I agree, [company_name] should include this in the user manual. It's frustrating and unfortunate that it took so long to discover.
Since I do not use the app, I have to rely solely on the manual when helping other users.

analysis.insight_summary: Users trying to set up push button functionality with the [product_name] app for Android and [product_name] [version_no] discover that only static switching is natively supported. The lack of detailed documentation leads to confusion and users turn to forum support to fill in missing information. There is shared frustration about the [company_name] manual not covering important scenarios for app usage.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the app to directly support push button behavior for digital inputs, and they look for comprehensive instructions in the official manual.
